title: The (Better) Case For European Banks
gist: Gavekal argues the four-year run of European bank stocks outperforming US banks in US dollar terms since 2022 has further to go: the sector is no longer at distressed valuations, but with earnings outlooks solid on both sides of the Atlantic, the European-versus-US valuation gap can still close.

themes.theme: European vs US bank relative trade

insights.claim: European bank stocks have outperformed their US counterparts in US dollar terms since 2022, ending more than a decade of underperformance.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The Europe-over-US bank pair trade is already a four-year-old winner; late entrants must judge whether the easy re-rating is behind them.
insights.quote: European bank stocks have now had four good years, outperforming their US counterparts since 2022 in US dollar terms
insights.locator: After more than a decade in the wilderness

insights.claim: Gavekal expects European bank stocks to keep outperforming US banks, arguing that even though the sector is no longer priced at distressed levels there is still room for European valuations to improve relative to US ones while earnings outlooks on both sides stay solid.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Stay long European banks against US banks; the thesis is now a valuation-convergence trade rather than a deep-value bounce.
insights.quote: The short answer is yes. European bank stocks are no longer priced at distressed levels. But with the earnings outlooks for European and US banks both solid, there is still room for European valuations to improve compared with the US.
insights.locator: The question is whether this outperformance

insights.claim: The bull case for European banks has shifted from a rebound off distressed pricing to a pure relative-valuation catch-up versus US peers, which means the remaining upside depends on multiple expansion rather than on cheapness alone.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch the European-vs-US bank price-to-book and P/E gap as the key mark-to-market on the thesis, since earnings surprise is no longer the main lever.
insights.locator: European bank stocks are no longer priced

themes.theme: Nominal growth and rates as the earnings driver

insights.claim: The initial driver of European banks' relative performance turnaround from 2022 was an acceleration in earnings and returns on equity versus the US bank sector as Europe escaped the deflationary overhang of the 2010s, with both nominal growth and interest rates rising.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The trade is levered to European nominal growth and positive rates; a slide back toward deflation or zero rates would remove the engine behind the outperformance.
insights.quote: an acceleration in earnings and returns on equity compared with the US bank sector as Europe emerged from the deflationary overhang of the 2010s, with nominal growth and interest rates both rising
insights.locator: The relative performance of European bank stocks began

themes.theme: Sentiment lag and the value-trap discount

insights.claim: Even as European bank earnings accelerated, investor expectations that the sector would remain a value trap caused it to derate over 2022-23 both against its own history and relative to US banks.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Improving fundamentals were absorbed by falling multiples, so the unwind of that sentiment discount is the specific source of future returns to monitor.
insights.quote: Expectations that European banks would remain a value trap meant that over 2022-23 the sector continued to derate both against its own historical record and relative to US banks
insights.locator: But the wilderness years cast a long shadow

insights.claim: Gavekal frames the European bank story as one where a long period of poor performance leaves a sentiment overhang that suppresses multiples well after the underlying earnings have inflected, creating a lag investors can exploit.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Applies beyond banks: screen for sectors where returns on equity have already turned but the multiple still reflects the previous regime.
insights.quote: But the wilderness years cast a long shadow.
